correctness.notes: oracle passed on every measured cell | 4 cells reported unsupported by the adapter's supported(), listed in correctness.unsupported_cells | phase 3 final evaluation, harness 0.10, nodes gb200-nvl4-ts2-99

low_level: Registers 32 to 80 over the 148 distinct kernels behind the card's cells (32 with register spills, a kernel measured in more than one batch counts once), shared memory 2432 to 20576 bytes, harness 0.10 on gb200-nvl4-ts2-99.
Adapter statics: input arrangement striped, output indices, temp storage 2400 to 4192 bytes.
Oracle battery (23 cases per cell plus the measurement seeds) passed on every cell that has a number, 4 cells unsupported by the adapter's contract or the device, no cell failed the oracle.
algorithmic: Random input (the one-node matrix on gb200-nvl4-ts2-99): latency prefer_smaller_index wins 2 of 39 cells (runner-up in 8), throughput prefer_smaller_index wins 18 of 39 cells (runner-up in 9).
Where it wins on random input (bf16 N 1024, bf16 N 4096, fp32 N 1024, fp32 N 4096, fp32 N 8192), the median margin over the runner-up is +6 percent and over the scope's reference control +30 percent.

Largest random-input deficits (distinct cells, worst regime): bf16 N 1024 k 4 +414 percent behind B2_packed@T128 in latency prefer_smaller_index, bf16 N 4096 k 4 +409 percent behind B2_twolevel in latency prefer_smaller_index, bf16 N 4096 k 8 +207 percent behind B2_packed in latency prefer_smaller_index, fp32 N 4096 k 4 +196 percent behind B2_twolevel in latency prefer_smaller_index.
Named workloads won on random input: dsa_small_context_8k_k2048, dsa_v32_merge_m4_k2048, dsa_v4_merge_m8_k1024.
negative: The GB200 pass measured random input only on one host (gb200-nvl4-ts2-99): the tie_heavy, shuffled-tie and phase 3b order-check findings for this adapter are on its B200 card.
surprises: det3 and det2 ran in the same GB200 pass on one host: over the 39 random cells where both have a value det3 is between 5 percent ahead and 2 percent behind B1_det2 in latency, and ahead in throughput at N 8192 for fp32 k 1024 and 2048 under prefer_smaller_index (510 to 541 against 385 to 392 Gelem/s), the cells where it is the winner.
open_questions: The bf16 deterministic price at N 8192 and above.

B200 pass (WINNERS_b200.md, random input on umbriel-b200-047, tie_heavy on 068, shuffled ties on 094, phase 3b on 047): the warp and sub-warp winners agree with GB200 on 359 of 376 common cells (365 of 376 when each cell is compared through the adapters both passes measured, as section 16 of the knowledge base does), the differences are named sub-warp lane-count cells, N 128 sub-warp throughput cells and warp ties within 5 percent, and in the block matrices the B1_idx against B1_det2 throughput ties fall either way. On GB200 the k 64 cells at 128 threads run 3 to 15 percent slower than on B200 (hw-researcher, a generation property) and the aarch64 cicc emits branches for the conditional swaps (T20, 3 to 4 percent).
